chunks: Muḥammad ibn Ziyād al-Azdī narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān al-Aḥmar, from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad:
A man came to him and said to him, “May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, teach me an admonition.”

So he عليه السلام said to him: “If Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has guaranteed sustenance, then why your anxiety? If sustenance is apportioned, then why greed? If reckoning is true, then why accumulation? If recompense from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is true, then why miserliness? If punishment from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the Fire, then why disobedience? If death is true, then why rejoicing? If presentation before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is true, then why deceit? If Shayṭān is an enemy, then why heedlessness? If passing over the Ṣirāṭ is true, then why self-admiration? If everything is by the decree and ordainment of Allah, then why grief? And if the world is perishing, then why feel at ease with it?”

key_terms.الصِّرَاطِ: the bridge/path that must be crossed in the afterlife
key_terms.الْحِسَابُ: the reckoning of deeds before Allah
key_terms.الْخَلَفُ: divine recompense or replacement from Allah for what is spent

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام explain the contradiction between belief in Allah and attachment to worldly anxieties?
ai.summary: This hadith is a concise ethical exhortation from Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that links belief in core truths—rizq, reckoning, death, the Fire, divine decree, and the fleeting nature of the world—to the abandonment of blameworthy traits. It teaches that sincere conviction should reshape conduct, reducing greed, deceit, heedlessness, and attachment to the dunya.
